messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert: net/transit SFO -> provider-q high packet loss and BGP flaps detected (AS path changes frequent). alert_id=PD-654321
pagerduty: #oncall alex.m paged (network)
alex.m: on it, looking at telemetry now. seeing 30-40% pktloss to some prefixes via provider-q egress from SFO.
alex.m: digging into BGP state: flapping updates from AS65040, multiple withdraws then re-ads.
alex.m: paste: ```bgp# show bgp ipv4 unicast summary
Neighbor        V    AS MsgRcvd MsgSent   TblVer  InQ OutQ Up/Down State/PfxRcd
192.0.2.5       4 65040  12034   12036        0    0    0 00:12:34  1024
192.0.2.6       4 65040  11890   11892        0    0    0 00:11:50  987
```
sasha.n: I see the same in our flow logs, a subset of customer prefixes are being routed through provider-q -> provider-x causing asymmetric paths and DNS query timeouts for some regions.
jamal: @alex.m any signs of upstream route leak vs transit maintenance?
alex.m: looks like an unintentional prepended path from provider-q into provider-x, causing their route reflectors to prefer a longer path intermittently -> oscillation. not a planned maintenance as far as providers' status pages.
irene: paging provider-q NOC, forwarding BGP timestamps and community tags. contact: noc@provider-q.example / +1-555-0123.
incident-bot: Incident created INC-2026-98 (network transit) — priority P1. Notification: #all-hands oncall and network.
alex.m: temporary mitigation options: 1) withdraw specific announce to provider-q for the effected prefixes from our side (risky), 2) prefer alternate transit by altering local-preference for those prefixes so traffic leaves via provider-r, 3) engage provider-q to fix upstream. leaning towards 2 to avoid global withdraws.
sasha.n: agree prefer option 2. I'll prep a route-policy change to bump local-pref for customer-prefixes towards provider-r.
taylor.r: I'm taking over triage (2nd shift). Alex handing off now. @team, can you document the exact prefixes impacted and customer-facing list?
alex.m: handing off to @taylor.r — notes: affected prefixes: 203.0.113.0/24, 198.51.100.0/22, 192.0.2.0/23. symptoms: packet loss, DNS timeouts for regional EU->SFO flows, elevated TCP retransmits.
jamal: support-bot run eval on customer error rates across services for those prefixes.
support-bot: Running query... results: increased error rates for embeddings API in eu-west (3x baseline) between 16:08-16:42 UTC; several customer sessions timed out, no data exfil. See internal dashboard: https://console.redwood.internal/d/net/PD-654321
taylor.r: applying local-pref adjustment to prefer provider-r for those prefixes. config snippet: ```policy-statement PREFER_PROVIDER_R {
  term 10 {
    from prefix-list AFFECTED
    then local-preference 200
  }
}
```
taylor.r: pushed change to edge routers in SFO, awaiting convergence (~2m).
sasha.n: seeing decreased traffic to provider-q on those prefixes. packet loss dropping to <1% for affected flows.
jamal: contacting support to notify affected customers. tagging severity and suggested workaround (retry, use eu-central region).
irene: provider-q acked receipt and says they're investigating an internal route-reflector bug. they're tracking as PROVQ-1128. asked for BGP update dumps.
alex.m: logging commands sent to provider and BGP dumps attached to provider ticket. also captured pcap snippets for 1 flow.
sasha.n: note: DNS cached entries caused lingering failures; recommend increasing TTL flush on sensitive records and issue advisory to customers.
taylor.r: rolled back partial withdraws (we only changed local-pref). no global withdraws performed.
jamal: support update posted: "We are seeing intermittent packet loss for traffic transiting provider-q from SFO. We have rerouted affected prefixes to alternate transit and packet loss is decreasing. Engineers are monitoring. For impacted requests, retrying requests or switching to regional endpoints (eu-central) should help." :warning:
irene: request for incident commander for postmortem: @alex.m or @taylor.r?
alex.m: happy to be incident commander for bridge and writeup, @taylor.r will handle next-steps ops notes.
incident-bot: on-call rotation reminder: next handoff at 18:00 UTC to oncall-net-east.
sasha.n: provider-q reports partial mitigation at 16:58 UTC, they have applied a fix to their route-reflectors, flows look stable.
taylor.r: monitoring shows stability for 35m, no new flaps. packet loss baseline restored.
jamal: final customer impact assessment draft: "~4k requests failed across 12 customers between 16:05-16:50 UTC; highest impact on embeddings API in eu-west, transient DNS failures observed; no data loss; mitigation performed by rerouting to alternate transit provider and provider-q applied internal fix."
irene: will create INC-2026-98 postmortem ticket and schedule 1h RCA tomorrow. action items: validate reroute policies, add BGP dampening threshold alerts, request provider postmortem from provider-q, update runbook for similar events.
alex.m: good job team. closing incident channel when support update is sent and metrics stable for 1h. :thumbsup:
support-bot: Customer notification sent to affected customers (ticket refs appended).
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-98 status: monitoring -> resolved (16:52 UTC) after provider fix and our reroute.
